name: Runway
h1: Runway ARR: $200M, Doubled in Five Months.
intro: Runway's annual recurring revenue hit $200 million in September 2026 — roughly double where it stood five months earlier — confirmed by co-CEO Anastasis Germanidis and reported by Bloomberg. Enterprise expansion with net revenue retention above 300% carried the ramp. Every reported figure below is traced to a public source.
metaTitle: Runway ARR: $200M Revenue, MRR and Growth Timeline (2026)

milestones.note: Estimated run rate in the tens of millions as Gen-2 subscriptions and early API access monetized; Runway pivoted the company fully to generative video.
Growth into the tens of millions of ARR on Gen-3 Alpha, with film-industry adoption (The Oscar-winning 'Everything Everywhere' VFX lineage) and enterprise pilots expanding.
Approaching ~$100M annualized by year-end as Gen-4 shipped and enterprise contracts scaled; a ~$400M round priced the company in the $3–5B range.

milestones.label: Apr–May '26
milestones.note: Crossed ~$100M ARR — the milestone that, per Bloomberg-reported figures, doubled to $200M within five months.

milestones.label: Sep '26
milestones.note: Co-CEO Anastasis Germanidis confirmed $200M ARR, roughly doubling in five months. Net revenue retention above 300%; one Fortune 20 customer grew usage 17x.

modelTitle: How Creator Credits Compound Into Enterprise Contracts.
modelParagraphs: Runway monetizes through two engines. Self-serve subscriptions for creators and creative teams run from roughly $12–15/month entry plans to ~$76–95/month unlimited-tier options, billed by credits for video generations. On top, the API sells Gen-4 and Aleph models per second of generated video to developers, ad agencies and media platforms.

The 2026 acceleration is enterprise-led: management credits net revenue retention above 300% — driven by customers expanding from pilots into production pipelines — with one Fortune 20 customer scaling usage 17x. Advertising and entertainment budgets, not individual creators, now carry the growth.
revenueMix: Credit-based plans from roughly $12–15/month up to ~$95/month unlimited tiers.
Gen-4 and Aleph models billed per second of video for developers and platforms.
300%+ net retention; a Fortune 20 customer grew usage 17x.

faqs.a: $200 million in annual recurring revenue as of September 2026, confirmed by co-CEO Anastasis Germanidis and reported by Bloomberg — roughly double the ~$100M level of five months earlier.

ARR doubled in roughly five months (about $100M in April–May 2026 to $200M in September). The ramp is enterprise-led, with net revenue retention above 300% and one Fortune 20 customer growing usage 17x.

Credit-based subscriptions for creators (roughly $12–15/month entry, up to ~$95/month unlimited tiers), a per-second API for its Gen-4 and Aleph video models, and direct enterprise contracts with media and advertising companies.
About $5.3 billion as of 2026, on roughly $400 million of total funding raised — pricing the company at about 26x its current ARR.

faqs.q: How Does Runway Compare With Other AI Video Companies?
faqs.a: Runway's disclosed $200M ARR is the largest confirmed figure among AI video startups — ahead of Luma's ~$80M estimate and OpenAI's Sora, which is not separately reported. Luma's $4B and Runway's $5.3B valuations are in a similar range.
